mutations.because: D212: the disposition on `outputDownloadUrl` is the WHOLE reason the field exists. `<a download>` is ignored for a cross-origin target and a presigned URL is on the store's origin by definition, so with the disposition dropped the download button opens the PNG in a new tab instead of saving it — the exact failure D209(d) left open and D212 closes. The filename is asserted as `attachment; filename="1x1.png"` on the path's OWN last segment, not merely as a non-null header, because a disposition that named the campaign or the product would satisfy a presence check and still save a file no user recognises. Only this lane's own test fails: the sibling `proofUrl`/`htmlBundleUrl` dispositions are untouched by this mutation.
command: outputDownloadUrl: attachment under the path's own last segment

mutations.because: D212's fs half: the download fields ARE the display fields on fs, byte for byte. There is no store to sign a disposition with, `<a download>` works same-origin, and the output route has no query that would carry one — so a second, differing string here would be a URL the server can only answer correctly by accident, and a web client would hold a link that resolves to bytes it cannot name. The mutation is subtle because it looks like a fix: it threads the disposition through as a query the route ignores, which keeps the path right and the string wrong. TWO of this lane's tests fail: the new 'on fs the download fields are byte-for-byte outputUrl/videoUrl' (which exists to state the D212 invariant in the fs direction) and PT-4f's own fs test at signed-urls.test.ts:230, because `proofUrl` and `htmlBundleUrl` carry a disposition too and would lose their `?v=` revision at the same time.
command: on fs the download fields are byte-for-byte outputUrl/videoUrl

mutations.because: D213: the re-read is what every completed run commits from, and restoring a gate around it reinstates the defect the plan recorded — a fresh Generate skips the read and commits the JOB payload, which the jobs route answers exactly as stored. That payload carries no `*Url` at all (`withAssetUrls` runs on `result.get` alone), so every creative on screen would have to be told where its bytes are by the client, which is a 404 under `s3`. The failing test is the STATE-level D213 (a) 'after Generate the tile shows result.get\'s outputUrl, not the job\'s', which pins the committed row on two fields the job payload differs on — the result route's `outputUrl` and its compliance score — so a commit from the job snapshot fails on the score too and not only on the field D213 is about. A grid test asserting a rendered `src` cannot see this: the consumers are PT-4g2's and still build their own URLs, so the tile would look identical either way.
command: after Generate the tile shows result.get's outputUrl, not the job's
